knowledge:
- key_parameters: n=number of clones or insertions in multinomial modeling ;; p=vector of multinomial probabilities (e.g., gene or target sizes) ;; iter=number of iterations for Monte Carlo approximation or bootstrap estimation ;; seed=random seed for reproducibility in Monte Carlo/bootstrap ;; alpha=significance level for confidence intervals ;; TR=logical flag for tracing/tracking in bootstrap functions ;; orf=matrix of ORF start and end coordinates ;; clone=vector of insertion positions
- alternatives: negenes package (similar functionality but uses a different data format; occugene provides occup2Negenes to convert data for compatibility)
- when_to_use: When analyzing random transposon mutagenesis libraries in prokaryotes to estimate the number of essential genes and predict future knockout rates.
- pitfalls: The bootstrap estimators (unbiasDelta0, unbiasB0) can be computationally intensive, and using too few iterations (e.g., iter=10 in examples) may yield imprecise confidence intervals. The input format requires tracking the exact order and coordinates of insert locations, which differs from negenes.

workflows.name: essential_gene_and_knockout_estimation
workflows.intent: Estimate the number of essential genes and predict the number of new gene knockouts in future clones using experimental transposon insertion data and genome annotations.
input: annotation.csv (table containing ORF start and end coordinates)
insertions.csv (table containing genomic positions of transposon insertions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load genome annotation and insertion data ;; 2. Format ORF coordinates and clone insertion positions ;; 3. Estimate future knockouts using the Efron and Thisted estimator ;; 4. Fit a nonlinear regression model to cumulative knockouts ;; 5. Estimate future knockouts using the Will and Jacobs' bootstrap ;; 6. Estimate the number of essential genes using the Will and Jacobs' bootstrap ;; 7. Convert data to negenes format if compatibility is needed
workflows.code:
data(sampleAnnotation)
data(sampleInsertions)
a.data <- sampleAnnotation
experiment <- sampleInsertions
orf <- cbind(a.data$first,a.data$last)
clone <- experiment$position
etDelta(10,orf,clone)
fFit(orf,clone,FALSE)
unbiasDelta0(10,orf,clone,iter=10,seed=4,alpha=0.05,TR=F)
unbiasB0(orf,clone,iter=10,seed=4,alpha=0.05,TR=F)
newOrf <- occup2Negenes(orf,clone)
